l.i: Non tutiori carcere VirginemSeruasse prudens Acrisius paterFertur, nec audacem catenaPirithoum grauior repressit.
Sed qui supremo Numine temperatOrbem, timores risit Ibericos:Custode quum iussit remotoClastra patere tibi reclusa.
Sic liberatum nunc precibus piaeGentis Nouaeum reddit amabilem:Uxoris & charum redonatFletibus egregiae maritum:
Qui magna ferret commoda patriae,Qui damna pulsis adderet hostibusDicenda, bellorum peritusMilite seu duce vellet uti,
Qui sceptra Princeps Gallica sustinet.Foecunda culpae secula nobilesOdere veros, atque honoreNon merito decorant inertes.
Te cura Christi provida recreetReddens solutis compedibus, nouaVirtuteque auctum nunc amatisAuxilium gregibus futurum,
Ardens recentis quos rabies LupiTerret pauentes, quum stabulis malumQua dissipatos nunc receptant

page.notes: The word at the lower right, "Saevior", is a catchword. Italic verse throughout; the line breaks within stanzas are marked with line breaks. Some letters are doubtful in the scan, notably "Ibericos" and "Acrisius"; the ligatures of the italic type are read as printed.
